name: Four of a Kind
description: Four of a Kind is a unique pokerndstyle betting game, traditionally played as a 'dealer's choice' option in home poker games. Unlike standard poker where you build a hand through drawing or communal cards, players in this game are each assigned a unique starting rank and wait for the deck to provide the matching cards. It is a game of high tension and split pots, where victory is divided between the first person to complete their set of four and the person holding the mathematically lowest hand at that moment.

history.origins: The game was documented by William Moore of New York, whose family introduced it as a 'poker night' variation in the late 1950s. It represents a genre of 'waiting games' where betting is driven by the visible progression of one's hand toward a fixed goal.
timeline: 1950s: First played in family poker circles in New York state.
1960s: Spread to college campuses as a social gambling game.
Present: Remains a niche but beloved 'wildcard' variant in home poker rotations.
history.cultural: Often played for small stakes (nickels and dimes), emphasizing the social aspect of 'waiting for your card' rather than calculated highndstakes bluffing.
history.evolution: The game simplifies the complex bluffing of poker into a straightforward race, using betting rounds to allow players to 'buy in' to their luck as matches appear.

setup.dealing: deal and betting Each player places the agreed ante into the pot.

rules.objective: Collect all four cards of your starting rank OR hold the lowest total hand when someone else completes their set.
rules.gameplay:
1. First Betting: After the initial cards are dealt, the player with the highest card starts the betting.
2. The Reveal: The dealer turns cards from the undealt deck one at a time.
3. Matching: If the turned card matches a player's rank, that player takes the card.
4. Betting Rounds: Every time a match occurs, a new round of betting begins, led by the player with the most cards (or highest rank if tied).
5. Discards: If a card doesn't match anyone's held rank, it is discarded, and the next card is flipped.

Round outcome is resolved by the scoring method: Scoring summary: Two-pot system: High pot (four-of-a-kind or best hand) and Low pot (lowest 5-card hand).
Winning condition: Collect all four cards of your starting rank OR hold the lowest total hand when someone else completes their set.

strategy.basic: If your starting rank is high (Aces or Kings), you can be more aggressive in early betting. If your rank is low, you should 'check' and 'call' to stay in the game for the Lowndpot half.
strategy.intermediate: The Fold Decision: If two cards of your rank are discarded early (because they were dealt as initial cards to others or flipped before you), you cannot win the Highndpot. You must then pivot to having the lowest total hand or fold to minimize losses.
strategy.advanced: Pot Odds: Calculate how many 'live' cards are left for your rank versus your opponents. If you have 3 cards and there is only 1 left in the deck, but your opponent has 1 and 3 left, your odds of hitting Four-of-a-Kind are significantly higher.
tips: Stay in if you have a low rank (2s or 3s) even if you aren't getting matches; you are the favorite for the Lowndhalf of the pot.
Fold early if you have a midndrange card (7s or 8s) and you aren't getting matches, as you are unlikely to win either the High or the Low pot.

scoring.description: Two-pot system: High pot (four-of-a-kind or best hand) and Low pot (lowest 5-card hand). Split at showdown.
scoring.winCondition: At showdown, High pot goes to best standard hand; Low pot goes to lowest 5-card hand (Ace-low). Splits possible if same player wins both.

synthesis.shortDescription: A poker-style vying game where players race to collect four cards of their assigned rank while betting on their progress, with the pot split between the four-of-a-kind winner and the holder of the lowest hand.
